hero.title: “Activities for <accent>all ages.</accent>”
hero.text: For some fifteen years, I have been organizing and leading community and educational programs on healthy eating. Here are the four programs I offer to schools, childcare services, non-profit organizations and businesses.

healthPromotion.title: Healthy eating promotion
healthPromotion.p1: At every stage of life, food plays a key role in your well-being and that of your loved ones. I invite you to revisit your eating habits in a playful way and find solutions that fit your lifestyle. Reviewing and adapting your eating habits over time is a source of renewed energy.
healthPromotion.p2: The birth of a baby, a child starting school, retirement, a new health diagnosis or an allergy-prone background can all call for changes.
themes: Planning and putting together balanced menus
Choosing foods and grocery store tours
Understanding the nutritional value of foods

cinqEpices.title: Ateliers cinq épices Alberta
cinqEpices.approach: Every child handles, measures and cuts the food. By cooking and tasting, our little chefs learn the basics of healthy eating, discover new foods and build independence in the kitchen.
cinqEpices.approachQuote: “Hands-on skills that engage all five senses stimulate both the child’s cognitive and sensory development, in a festive, playful atmosphere that encourages discovery. The workshops are a learning experience in nutrition and the culinary arts focused on fun and sensory awakening, all aimed at promoting health.”
cinqEpices.mission: To promote nutrition and cooking education and encourage social development through food, for preschool and school-age children, their families and adults in general.

timeline.title: 2003, Les Ateliers cinq épices are born
timeline.text: Les Ateliers cinq épices were founded in Montréal, Quebec, to promote nutrition and cooking education for children (aged 2 to 12) and their families.

timeline.title: 2015 to 2020, a pilot project in Alberta
timeline.text: The ACFA régionale de Calgary partners with CelineCestBon to bring the Ateliers cinq épices program to Alberta. It becomes the first province to offer these workshops outside Quebec.

timeline.title: 2020 to 2026, adapting the program to Alberta
timeline.text: The project is aligned with Alberta Education standards and the principles of Health Promoting Schools.

timeline.title: 2026 to 2029, launch of the Ateliers cinq épices - Alberta program in its own right
timeline.text: A lasting program that adapts to Alberta for all young people (aged 2 to 12). The workshops are tailored to the children’s age, building the different skills they need to develop.

cinqEpices.historyText: The program highlights the collaboration of five key partners: children, parents, schools, the community and funders.
format: Small-group cooking workshops, led by a certified facilitator.

stats.title: Ten years later, the numbers speak for themselves

items.label: facilitators trained and certified in Alberta

stats.footnote: Not to mention 18 educators and 63 parent volunteers. Main regions visited: Calgary, Red Deer, Brooks and Fort McMurray.

collectiveKitchens.short: Community kitchens, from sharing to know-how
collectiveKitchens.title: Community kitchens
collectiveKitchens.tagline: “Sharing cooking know-how for the good of the community.”
collectiveKitchens.p1: These small-group workshops help community members rediscover cooking skills.
collectiveKitchens.p2: It’s a time to create healthy, budget-friendly recipes designed to respect cultural diversity, culinary traditions and any special health needs of participants and recipients. The workshops offer modules for all ages, from young children to seniors.
collectiveKitchens.p3: Held in small groups, these workshops encourage sharing skills and sharing and handing out the dishes prepared, in a friendly, educational setting that fosters new eating habits.
forWho: Members of community organizations (youth, adults, seniors, even intergenerational groups)
format: Tasting and/or handing out (how and how long to store food)

workplace.title: Healthy eating in the workplace
workplace.p1:
The average work week in Canada is about 35.8 hours (Statistics Canada). But during that time, food isn’t necessarily your priority. Whether you work at a large company or a small school, it’s important to build good eating habits.
So I offer breaks where we can talk about your needs and ways to fit the solutions into your day.
services: Planning meals around your work schedule
Organization and nutritional needs at events
Setting up a suitable space for meals
